name: Kherwadi Social Welfare Association
description: Kherwadi Social Welfare Association (KSWA) was founded in 1928 by Late Shri. B.G. Kher, a freedom fighter, statesman and the first Premier of Bombay State. He was moved by the plight and miserable living conditions of the 100 odd tanner families who had settled in the marshes of Bandra (E). While he was involved in the freedom struggle, leading two ministries in 1937 and 1946, interspersed with prison terms, his friends and associates started the Chamdewalla-ki-wadi in 1928 and continued to work in the area, which later came to be known as "Kherwadi".

Seed balls are one of the simplest reforestation tools, and one of the oldest.

What is a seed ball?

→ A small ball of clay, compost, and native seeds
→ Scattered across degraded land
→ Breaks open with the first rain, and the seedling grows

Why does it work?

→ Native seeds match the local ecosystem
→ The clay shell protects from birds, ants, and harsh sun
→ The compost feeds the seedling through its first weeks
→ Reaches land that conventional plantation cannot

Why does it count under CSR?

→ Aligned with Schedule VII activity 4: environmental sustainability and conservation of natural resources
→ Feeds directly into BRSR Core biodiversity disclosure
→ Hands-on, trackable, and CSR-2 documentation ready

Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals:

→ SDG 13: Climate Action
→ SDG 15: Life on Land
→ SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals

Every child deserves a safe childhood — a chance to learn, play, and grow without fear. The Protection of Child Rights Act and related laws aim to ensure every child in India grows up safe and educated. However, in 2025–2026 many children still face abuse, neglect, and exploitation despite legal safeguards.

What is the Protection of Child Rights Act in India?
The Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, also known as the Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, led to the establishment of the National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR and SCPCRs) frameworks, which monitor and safeguard child rights. Together with laws like POCSO and the Juvenile Justice Act, it protects children from abuse, labour, and discrimination.

name: Swades Foundation | Rural Empowerment
description: Swades Foundation, One of the Top NGOS in India working for rural empowerment. It works in four main areas of development which are Water & Sanitation, Health, Education and Livelihoods. This includes providing each home with access to a drinking water tap inside the house, an individual toilet, making primary healthcare accessible to the villagers, providing scholarships and faculties for school infrastructure, livelihood opportunities etc. In the year 2022, Swades Foundation has completed 75 dream villages project. A village qualifies as a Swades Dream Village by achieving over 40 parameters bucketed into 5 S's : Swachh(Clean),Sundar(Beautiful),Swasthya(Access to Healthcare),Sakshar(Educated) and Saksham(Self-Reliant)

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Yagnik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been immensely impressed by the Swades Foundation's work and their unwavering commitment to making a real difference in rural and tribal communities. Their work is not just genuine, but it's transformative. The impact they've had on the lives of those in need is nothing short of remarkable.

What sets Swades Foundation apart is their laser-focused goal – improving the lives of those living in underserved areas. This clarity of purpose ensures that every initiative, every project is meticulously designed to address the most pressing issues faced by these communities, be it Drinking water, sanitation, education, healthcare, or livelihood opportunities.

One of the standout features of Swades Foundation is their enthusiastic and dedicated team and management. Their passion for the cause is palpable, and it reflects in the results they achieve. They don't just implement projects; they invest in the empowerment of the people they serve.

In summary, Swades Foundation is a shining example of an organization that not only talks the talk but walks the walk. They are creating tangible, life-changing impacts, and their commitment to their mission is truly inspiring. This is the kind of organization that makes the world a better place, one rural and tribal life at a time. Kudos to the Swades Foundation!
